history.content: I farm monoculture wheat in a semi-arid region. My soil organic carbon has dropped to critically low levels (0.3%) and water availability is poor. How can I restore soil health and improve biodiversity while maintaining agricultural productivity?

Can you specify which sustainable practices you are open to adopting (e.g., cover cropping, reduced tillage, agroforestry, supplemental irrigation) and any constraints such as budget, equipment, or water rights?
agroforestry , and not having any such constraints

- Implement agrisilvicultural alley cropping by integrating rows of drought-resilient, nitrogen-fixing trees (e.g., Sesbania or Gliricidia) within your wheat fields to drive carbon input and shade the understory.
- Adopt conservation tillage and retain crop residues or organic mulch on the soil surface to drastically cut evaporation and suppress weeds.
- Incorporate legume cover crops during off-seasons to accelerate nitrogen cycling and boost labile soil organic carbon.
- Transition away from monoculture wheat to a diversified rotation incorporating crops compatible with the agroforestry setup to stimulate beneficial arbuscular mycorrhizal fungi.
